activity.notes: The scholar Abu Hanifa took over his Kufan mentor Hammad ibn Abi Sulayman's teaching circle after Hammad's death dated AH 120/c.737–738 CE, per Encyclopaedia Iranica. Records one scholarly succession event around 737 rather than a fabricated continuous 80-year teaching career. Kufa at this date lay within Umayyad-controlled Iraq; `active_in` does not imply service to the Umayyad state. His date of birth differs across later accounts; follow academically supported 699–767, not the NamuWiki page's 669.

sources.title: Abū Ḥanīfa — Encyclopaedia Iranica (Umar Faruq Abd-Allah, 1983; revised 2018)
sources.citation_text: Iranica reports teacher Hammad ibn Abi Sulayman's death in AH 120/737 CE and Abu Hanifa's eventual succession to his teaching circle, and gives Abu Hanifa's dates as 699–767.

sources.title: Hanafite Maḏhab — Encyclopaedia Iranica (Merlin Swartz, 2003)
sources.citation_text: Iranica describes Abu Hanifa as a leading eighth-century Kufan jurist, distinguishing his teachings from the later codification by his disciples.
